notes.meaning: Israel looked back at the land they won on the east side of the Jordan River before crossing over. These territories reached from the Arnon gorge in the south all the way north to Mount Hermon. God gave them these lands first as proof that He keeps His promises.

Sihon was an Amorite king who ruled from Heshbon over a large region, including half of Gilead and the eastern Jordan valley down to the Dead Sea. He refused to let Israel pass through in peace, so God gave him and his kingdom to Israel. Powerful rulers cannot stop what God has planned for His people.

King Og ruled Bashan from two royal cities, Ashtaroth and Edrei, and was one of the last of the giant Rephaim people. His realm reached north to Mount Hermon and covered the northern half of Gilead. Even though Og was feared and mighty, God gave Israel a complete victory over him.

Moses led Israel to defeat Sihon and Og and gave their land to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh. Joshua's newer victories did not replace the good work God had already done through Moses. God's people are called to remember past mercies even as they enjoy new ones.

The record turns to the west side of the Jordan River, where Joshua led Israel against many local kings. This territory included hills, valleys, desert lands, and fertile slopes once held by six Canaanite peoples. God gave all these diverse lands to the rest of Israel as their promised home.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many scholars compare this detailed list to ancient Near Eastern victory monuments, which kings set up to officially record conquered lands and show the success of their campaigns.

notes.meaning: The list of defeated western kings begins with Jericho and Ai, the first two cities conquered in central Canaan. It continues with Jerusalem and Hebron, whose kings led the southern alliance against Israel. God showed His power early by bringing down these major strongholds.

These verses name the kings of Jarmuth, Lachish, Eglon, and Gezer. The first three kings joined together to fight Israel in the south, while the king of Gezer came out to rescue Lachish. None of their armies could succeed because the Lord fought for Israel.

Joshua defeated the rulers of Debir, Geder, Hormah, and Arad in the southern country. Hormah and Arad sat near the southern desert where Israel had once been beaten years earlier during their wanderings. God now turned that place of past failure into a place of triumph.

This group includes the kings of Libnah, Adullam, Makkedah, and Bethel. Adullam was later known as the place with a cave where David hid, while Bethel stood near Ai in the hills. God cleared these enemy strongholds step by step so His people could live in peace.

The roster lists the rulers of Tappuah, Hepher, Aphek, and Lasharon. These city-states guarded key roads and fertile valleys across central Canaan. Overcoming them opened up the heart of the country for Israel.

These verses list the kings of Madon, Hazor, Shimron-meron, and Achshaph from the northern battles. Hazor had been the head of a huge alliance of northern kings that gathered to wipe out Israel. God gave Joshua victory over that entire northern coalition in a single campaign.

These kings ruled cities in the northwest, including Taanach, Megiddo, Kedesh, and Jokneam near Mount Carmel. Several of these towns were later set apart for the Levites or chosen as safe towns called cities of refuge. God took pagan royal towns and turned them into places that served His people.

The list finishes with the kings of Dor on the seacoast, Goiim in Gilgal, and Tirzah, bringing the total to thirty-one kings. In ancient times, a king often ruled just one fortified city and its nearby farms. Listing every single defeated king proved that God completely fulfilled His promise to give Israel the land.

differ.view: Some evangelicals explain that while Joshua broke the military power of all thirty-one kings, individual tribes still faced the task of clearing out the remaining Canaanites from their local settlements.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Scholars note that this roster closely matches the style of royal victory lists from other ancient nations, showing it was kept as an official historical record.
